daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo led a solemn reflection ceremony at TMP Kalibata ahead of Indonesia's 81st Independence Day. The president has also urged universities to participate in the construction of the Giant Sea Wall infrastructure project. Former President Jokowi voiced optimism over Prabowo's 2026 state address delivered on Independence Day.

  • The government has emphasized that food and energy self-reliance will anchor Indonesia's 2027 state budget planning.
  • The Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal and Security Affairs responded to incidents in which the Indonesian flag and Garuda emblem were removed in Aceh.
  • The government has called for peace in Aceh and security stability in Papua.
  • The DPR Task Force on Natural Disasters visited NTT to assess basic needs and permanent housing for earthquake victims.
  • The DPR has pledged to monitor the acceleration of handling for victims of the 7.7 magnitude NTT earthquake.
  • Ten members of the flag-hoisting honor guard (Paskibra) were inaugurated by the Indonesian Embassy in Beijing for Independence Day ceremonies.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Foreign Minister Sugiono appreciated the attention of friendly nations regarding the NTT earthquake disaster. Russia and the United Arab Emirates have expressed condolences over the NTT earthquake. The Indonesian Embassy in Beijing is hosting Indonesia Fair 2026 to showcase Indonesian culinary and cultural products in China.

  • The Indonesian Air Force has airlifted 13 tons of emergency aid to NTT earthquake-affected areas.
  • Indonesia is marketing Muntok white pepper to 1,200 restaurants globally.

Other

President Prabowo has guaranteed maximum assistance for victims of the NTT earthquake, which has now claimed at least 55 lives according to updated reports. The government prioritized rescue efforts during the emergency response phase, with the emergency period targeted to conclude within 2-3 weeks. The disaster has triggered 995 aftershocks, with 46 felt by residents.

  • The Ministry of Social Affairs has provided Rp15 million compensation to heirs of NTT earthquake victims and dispatched additional logistical aid via sea routes.
  • The Agriculture Minister has sent food assistance worth Rp75.4 billion for NTT earthquake victims.
  • PLN has restored Flores' main electricity supply following the earthquake.
  • Police arrested two Indian nationals who allegedly smuggled illegal gold to Dubai, with the network reportedly processing 30 kg of illegal gold daily worth nearly Rp3 trillion per month.
  • BRIN is developing an N219 aircraft ecosystem for a flying ambulance vision and coal waste-based battery technology for the electric vehicle ecosystem.

weekly_review.html:
President Prabowo proposed Destry Damayanti as sole candidate for Bank Indonesia governor and floated amnesty for SOE executives in his major annual address.

On Monday, August 10, Prabowo nominated acting governor Destry Damayanti as the only candidate to permanently lead Bank Indonesia following Perry Warjiyo's sudden resignation in late July, potentially making her the first woman to hold the post. The rupiah strengthened following the announcement, with markets relieved that concerns about central bank independence had been allayed. Later in the week, during his Friday speech at the annual MPR session, Prabowo floated creating an ad hoc court to investigate SOE executives over the past 30 years while also proposing amnesty for those who "repent" as part of a broader plan to close 750 unproductive state companies. On Saturday, State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi clarified that the proposal aimed at governance reform had not yet reached the amnesty stage, though coalition deputy speaker Dasco Ahmad said the idea needed further study as Prabowo was "too enthusiastic."

Celebrations marking 21 years of peace in Aceh descended into violence when crowds clashed with security forces over a crescent-star flag.

On Saturday, August 15, clashes erupted at Banda Aceh's Baiturrahman Grand Mosque during commemorations of Aceh Peace Day when an individual climbed a flagpole and lowered Indonesia's red-and-white flag to raise a crescent-star flag. TNI personnel on guard fired warning shots into the air when crowds attempted to raise the separatist banner, provoking stone-throwing and a chase of security forces toward the city parliament building. Several vehicles were damaged and at least one motorcycle was burned in the unrest. Army spokesman Major General Muhammad Nas called for all parties to respect state symbols and maintain order, while former vice president Jusuf Kalla urged restraint and emphasized the 21st anniversary as a moment to build justice and prosperity in Aceh.

Indonesia's navy conducted a passing exercise with China near Taiwan, drawing condemnation from Taipei and requests for clarification.

On Tuesday, August 12, China's defense ministry announced that Chinese and Indonesian naval vessels would conduct a joint navigation exercise in waters east of Taiwan, involving communications drills and at-sea replenishment. The exercise took place Wednesday morning between 6:30 a.m. and 9:30 a.m., roughly 70-80 nautical miles east of Taiwan, featuring Indonesia's frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai and China's Honghe. Taiwan's foreign ministry asked Indonesia for clarification and condemned China's behavior as creating a false impression of jurisdiction over the waters. Indonesian Navy spokesman First Admiral Tunggul explained that the exercise was routine maritime diplomacy conducted while the warship returned from Vladivostok, emphasizing that passing exercises are common goodwill engagements conducted by navies worldwide. Analysts noted this was the first foreign navy involvement since China began patrols off Taiwan's east coast in June.

commentary_review.html:
Writing in Fulcrum, Yanuar Nugroho argues that Indonesia's revised financial omnibus law reflects a broader trend towards executive recentralisation, with the central government reconsolidating authority through institutional control. The amendment to the P2SK Law expands Bank Indonesia's mandate while increasing parliamentary oversight, part of a pattern that includes regional budget cuts, sovereign wealth fund governance, and data regulation changes. Nugroho contends that institutions previously entrusted to protect long-term stability are now increasingly expected to deliver short-term political objectives, eroding the deliberate distribution of power established during Reformasi in the late 1990s.

Writing in Fulcrum, A'an Suryana argues that the leadership contest in Nahdlatul Ulama, Indonesia's largest Islamic organisation, is consequential for the country's political landscape. While there is no threat to NU's progressive and moderate ideology, the possibility of political realignment is real, particularly if Minister of Religious Affairs Nasaruddin Umar, who is closely aligned with President Prabowo, positions himself for the top job. The next executive chairman could either stay close to the President or respond to grassroots calls for change, with several candidates including incumbent Yahya Cholil Staquf competing for the position ahead of the August 2026 congress.

Writing in The Diplomat, Thijs Stegeman argues that China enlists foreign countries to support its increasingly strict interpretation of the One China principle, with Indonesia's recent joint naval exercise east of Taiwan providing a notable example. The August 2026 exercise marked the first time China had exercised with a foreign military in these geopolitically sensitive waters, which Chinese state media framed as demonstrating Beijing's sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the exclusive economic zone east of Taiwan. While Indonesia's Navy downplayed the significance of the drill as routine, the incident reflects a recent trend of China leveraging third countries to corroborate its jurisdictional claims, though it remains unclear whether Indonesia fully understood the sensitivity beforehand.

Writing in The Diplomat, Robin Vochelet argues that Indonesia's transgender community is facing growing repression following President Prabowo's October 2025 decree identifying the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture as a nonmilitary threat to national security. The decree represents a first step toward codifying anti-LGBTQ+ discrimination into federal law, using the language of securitization to justify this decision. A wave of hate crimes in July 2026 saw mobs attacking transgender women across the country, with researcher Febi Ramadhan noting that such attacks have become more frequent over the past decade, particularly during periods of economic turmoil when queer people are demonized to divert attention from other issues.
